title: Dedicated Capacity Throughput Verifier and Acceptance Playbook
creator: Sara Kline
description: Create a reproducible, customer-friendly throughput verification framework and playbook for Dedicated capacity. This ticket covers the load harness design, benchmarking methodology, and a concrete set of customer acceptance tests/signoff steps that will be used during Dedicated onboarding and SLA guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic load harness that can replay tenant-mix traffic and synthetic microbursts against a dedicated pool is checked into infra/benchmarks and can be run by non-engineers with documented steps.
Benchmark run produces a standard artifact (JSON + CSV) with token-level latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU utilization, queue depth, and cost-per-1000-tokens estimate.
Automated guardrails validate autoscaler behavior during ramp and sustained phases: no unnecessary scale-ups for short microbursts; scale-to targets within defined windows for sustained increases.
Customer acceptance checklist exists with pass/fail criteria mapped to SLA thresholds (throughput capacity, tail latency, error rate, and warmup time) and a sample signature run for customer signoff.
Playbook includes troubleshooting steps for common failure modes: KV-cache cold starts, model fallback, OOM, and noisy neighbors.
Benchmarking methodology is documented with statistical treatment (warmup, repeats, confidence intervals) and reproducible seed/config files used for RFCs/releases.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design harness API and canonical scenario definitions (tenant-mix, steady-state sustain, microburst injection, tail-focused traces).
Phase 2: Implement harness as containerized runner with YAML scenario configs, metrics exporter, and optional replay driver for customer traces (scrubbed).
Phase 3: Integrate with CI to run smoke benchmarks on staging; add an endpoint in Console for uploading signature-run artifacts for customer review.
Phase 4: Validate autoscaling policies using synthetic ramp profiles; iterate on safety knobs (min-instances, cooldowns, max-burst-capacity).
Phase 5: Produce a customer-facing runbook and run two pilot onboarding sessions with existing Dedicated customers for feedback.
benchmarking_methodology: Workload taxonomy: define 3 canonical workload profiles — interactive low-latency, sustained throughput (high tokens/sec), and bursty mixed-tenant replay.
Warmup & priming: run a warmup phase per-run to populate KV cache; measure and report warmup duration and its impact on tail latency.
Repetition and CI: execute at least 5 independent runs per scenario, compute mean and 95% CI for p95/p99; report run-to-run variance.
Statistical rules: discard first warmup run when estimating steady-state, require coefficient of variation < 10% for throughput claims or increase sample size.
Cost normalization: measure total GPU seconds and map to per-1000-token cost using current pricing models; include cost sensitivity to batch-size and quantization.
Failure injection: include optional network latency jitter and node-termination signals to validate graceful fallback and autoscaler recovery.
load_harness_architecture: Runner: Go-based microservice that reads YAML scenarios and schedules request streams with tenant-id multiplexing.
Scenario configs: declarative profiles for request distribution, prompt lengths, KV-cache warmup traces, and client-side concurrency.
Observability: built-in Prometheus exporter that emits token_latency_seconds (histogram), request_errors, queue_depth, gpu_utilization, and batch_sizes.
Replay support: optional sanitized-trace ingestion to reproduce customer traffic shape; supports mapping to tenant-weighted mixes.
Orchestration: container + Helm chart used to spin test generator in same region as Dedicated pool; supports ephemeral VPC peering for private deployments.
Artifacts: standardized output bundle (bench-results.json + trace-logs.tar.gz + grafana-snapshot-link).
customer_acceptance_tests: Signature run: run the canonical customer scenario with their representative prompts (scrubbed) and produce an artifact for the customer to review within 24 hours.
SLA validation: verify the Dedicated pool sustains contract throughput for 30 minutes with p99 latency under the SLA target and error rate < 0.1%.
Autoscaler behavior: execute scripted ramp (2x -> 5x sustained) and check scale events, cooldown adherence, and absence of oscillation; record scale latency.
Warmup confirmation: measure time-to-steady-state from cold start and provide recommendations (min-instances or proactive priming) if warmup exceeds acceptable window.
Fallback resilience: during a controlled node failure, confirm automatic fallback to configured model variant or region maintains degraded-but-serviceable throughput.
Customer signoff: runbook includes a checkbox-driven signoff form where PM, customer SE, and SRE certify the artifact and mark PASS/FAIL with notes.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Replay traces may leak sensitive data. Mitigation: provide scrubbers and mandatory review before uploading; default to synthetic seeds if review missing.
Risk: Benchmarks overfit to synthetic workload and mispredict customer extremes. Mitigation: require at least one real (sanitized) customer trace or close-analogue scenario for final signoff.
Risk: Autoscaler flaps during microbursts causing cost blowouts. Mitigation: implement microburst detection and short-burst admission control with configurable burst budget.
Risk: Customers misinterpret CI-smoke numbers as guarantees. Mitigation: clearly label artifacts as 'as-run' with exact config and confidence intervals; provide recommended guardrails for production.
observability_and_metrics: Mandatory metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, requests/sec, tokens/sec, GPU% utilization, batch_size distribution, queue_depth, error_rate.
Derived metrics: cost_per_1k_tokens, steady_state_throughput, warmup_loss (delta between first and steady p95), autoscale_event_rate.
Dashboards: provide a per-run Grafana template that highlights tail latency, GPU headroom, and per-tenant throughput; add URL to artifact bundle.
Logging: standardized trace IDs and sample payload capture with redaction rules; ensure logs include model variant, kernel selection, and quantization profile.
